blocks.narration: Roth or traditional? Choosing the right retirement account comes down to one simple question about taxes. Here it is.
blocks.visual: A clay fork in the road with two glowing signposts, one gold and one silver

blocks.narration: With a traditional account, your contributions may lower your taxable income today. You pay income tax later, when you withdraw.
blocks.visual: A clay figure carries a lighter backpack now, but a toll booth waits far down the road

blocks.narration: With a Roth, you contribute money you already paid tax on. Qualified withdrawals in retirement come out completely tax-free.
blocks.visual: The figure pays a small toll at the start, then strolls freely down an open road

blocks.narration: So the question is this. Do you expect your tax rate to be higher now, or higher in retirement?
blocks.visual: A clay seesaw tips back and forth between a young figure and an older figure

blocks.narration: If you expect to be in a higher bracket later, paying tax now with a Roth can win. If lower later, traditional can win.
blocks.visual: The seesaw settles one way, then the other, with gold coins sliding to the lower side

blocks.narration: Roth growth is never taxed once rules are met, and Roth I R As have no required withdrawals during the owner's lifetime.
blocks.visual: A clay tree grows tall inside a glass dome, untouched by falling rain

blocks.narration: Many people split their contributions between both types as a hedge, since nobody knows what future tax rates will be.
blocks.visual: Two jars side by side both receive coins, one gold and one silver

blocks.narration: Roth I R As have income limits, so check the current rules before choosing. Follow so you do not miss the next retirement explainer.
blocks.visual: The two roads merge into one sunny path as the camera pulls back

captions.hook_line: Roth or traditional? It comes down to one question ⚖️
captions.body: Traditional accounts can lower taxes now and tax withdrawals later. Roth accounts use after-tax money, and qualified withdrawals are tax-free. The better choice depends on your tax rate now versus in retirement.

youtube_title: Roth vs Traditional: Which One Wins?
